title: Towards Next Graph Token Prediction: Discrete Graph Tokenization for Structural Reasoning in Large Language Models

problem.claim: Extending autoregressive next-token prediction to graph data requires next graph token prediction that supports structural reasoning.

gap.claim: Existing graph tokenizations struggle to capture higher-order structural semantics with high information density while remaining strictly reversible; textual encodings are long and semantically sparse, whereas continuous encodings lose exact topology.

contributions.claim: GraphVulcan is a framework for discrete, reversible, semantically rich graph tokenization using a vocabulary of canonical graphlets.
The framework uses a three-stage training paradigm consisting of structural semantic pretraining, multi-task fine-tuning on CoT-augmented reasoning examples, and reinforcement learning.
GraphVulcan enables graph-level next-token prediction over compositional graphlets for structural reasoning by LLMs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GraphVulcan as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GraphVulcan outperforms first-order encoding baselines across seven graph reasoning tasks and three real-world benchmarks.
The authors report higher computational efficiency relative to first-order encoding baselines.
The authors report that structure-aware discrete tokenization is feasible for general-purpose graph-language models capable of structural reasoning.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities through autoregressive next-token prediction.
Applying next-token prediction to graphs requires tokenizations that jointly capture structural semantics and preserve exact reversibility.
GraphVulcan addresses this problem with canonical graphlet vocabulary and discrete reversible semantic-rich tokenization.
The approach trains through structural semantic pretraining, multi-task fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.
The authors report improvements over first-order encoding baselines on graph reasoning tasks and real-world benchmarks, along with higher computational efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The proposed tokenization combines canonical graphlets with reversibility and semantic richness.

interpretation.claim: For structured data reasoning, a representation may need to preserve exact structure while exposing reusable compositional units.

application.claim: When designing structured-data interfaces for language models, evaluate both semantic expressiveness and lossless reconstruction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this representation generalizes beyond the reported graph reasoning tasks and benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the seven graph reasoning tasks or three real-world benchmarks.
No quantitative results, evaluation metrics, or computational-efficiency measurements are provided.
The abstract does not specify the canonical graphlet vocabulary, tokenization algorithm, or reversibility evaluation.
The abstract does not provide training data sizes, model configurations, or ablation results.
